lines.text: Here's the new product page we're testing, and what changes for shoppers.
Product photos are sharper. The photography was always good; the current page loads a small copy and stretches it.
On the current page, every option change covers the page with a spinner, and you wait.
The new page swaps the photo, price and stock the moment you click, so you can flip between colors.
Options are labeled, and a dashed border marks what's out of stock. You can still pick one, and ask for a back-in-stock email.
If a combination doesn't exist, the page says so, and lists what is available.
Any option with a long list of choices now has a search box. Typing blue narrows these inks to seventeen, and each shows its picture.
The current page is a long list of names, with no pictures to go by.
Pick one, and its picture shows in the field and in the main photo.
And Build a mixed order puts several colors in one order.
The current page just says Sale. The new one shows the percent off for each option, and updates as you switch.
When buying more doesn't save anything, it says so: no volume discount on this option.
The quantity now looks like a box you can type in. In recordings, shoppers missed that and tapped plus over and over.
At five, the new page shows the volume price, a dollar sixty each, where the current page still shows two dollars.
The current bulk view is one long list. Now you can search it, filter by option, and show only sale items.
Sale rows show their savings, and an itemized summary builds as you enter quantities.
The current Reset is a big button that clears everything in one click. The new one is a small link that asks first.

Over fifteen days, shoppers added about one point one million dollars to carts one item at a time, and eighty-four thousand through bulk. We suspect that's because bulk is hard to use. The test now counts how often shoppers open it, so we'll find out.
On phones, a bar keeps the price and a way back to your options in reach as you scroll.
In bulk, the rows scroll with the page and the total stays pinned. On the current page, you scroll inside a separate box.
